plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following losses cannot be set off against any other head of income in the same assessment year under the Income-tax Act, 1961?
options: Business loss of a specified business referred to in section 35AD
Loss from an ordinary non-speculative business
plain.explanation: As per section 73A, any loss computed in respect of any specified business referred to in section 35AD can be set off only against profits and gains, if any, of any other specified business. It cannot be set off against income under any other head.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under section 70, inter-source adjustment is generally permissible. Which of the following inter-source adjustments is NOT allowed?
options: Loss from house property A set off against income from house property B
Loss from a speculative business set off against profit from an ordinary business
Loss from an ordinary business set off against income from a speculative business
Loss from a non-speculative business set off against income from house property
plain.explanation: Under section 73(1), any loss computed in respect of a speculative business carried on by the assessee cannot be set off except against profits and gains of another speculative business. Thus, it cannot be set off against ordinary business profits.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the maximum period for which business loss (other than speculation loss and specified business loss) can be carried forward and set off under section 72?
plain.explanation: Under section 72(3), business loss can be carried forward for a maximum of 8 assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year for which the loss was first computed.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a loss from an activity of owning and maintaining race horses be set off against income from salary in the same assessment year?
options: No, it cannot be set off against income under any other head, nor can it be set off against any other source under the head Income from Other Sources
Yes, subject to a limit of Rs. 2,00,000
Yes, if the assessee maintains regular books of accounts
plain.explanation: Under section 74A(3), the loss incurred in the activity of owning and maintaining race horses can be set off only against income from the same activity i.e., owning and maintaining race horses. It cannot be set off against any other head or source.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In the case of a company (other than a company in which public are substantially interested), unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward:
options: Indefinitely, even if there is a change in shareholding
Indefinitely, subject to the provisions of section 79
plain.explanation: As per section 32(2), unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward indefinitely and has no time limit. Unlike business losses, unabsorbed depreciation is not subject to the change in shareholding restrictions under section 79.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: For carrying forward and setting off of accumulated business losses in case of closely held companies, what percentage of voting power must remain continuously beneficially held under section 79?
plain.explanation: Section 79 provides that in case of a company in which public are not substantially interested, loss incurred in any year prior to the previous year can be carried forward only if not less than 51% of the voting power is beneficially held by the same persons on the last day of the previous year.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following losses can be carried forward even if the return of income is filed after the due date specified under section 139(1)?
plain.explanation: As per section 80 read with section 139(3), filing the return of income within the due date under section 139(1) is mandatory for carrying forward business loss, speculation loss, specified business loss, and capital loss. However, loss under the head 'Income from house property' and unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward even if the return is filed late.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the maximum period for carrying forward capital losses (both short-term and long-term) under section 74?
plain.explanation: Under section 74(1) and 74(2), both short-term capital losses and long-term capital losses can be carried forward for a maximum of 8 assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year in which the loss was first computed.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a long-term capital loss be set off against short-term capital gains in the same assessment year?
options: No, long-term capital loss can only be set off against long-term capital gains
Yes, long-term capital loss can be set off against both short-term and long-term capital gains
No, capital losses cannot be set off against capital gains at all
Yes, but only up to Rs. 1,00,000
plain.explanation: Under section 70(3), a long-term capital loss can be set off against any capital gain, whether short-term or long-term. However, a short-term capital loss can be set off against both short-term and long-term capital gains as well.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the order of priority for setting off unabsorbed depreciation, current year business loss, and brought forward business loss?
options: Current year business loss -> Brought forward business loss -> Unabsorbed depreciation
Current year business loss -> Unabsorbed depreciation -> Brought forward business loss
Unabsorbed depreciation -> Current year business loss -> Brought forward business loss
Brought forward business loss -> Current year business loss -> Unabsorbed depreciation
plain.explanation: The order of set-off under the Act is: (1) Current year deductions like depreciation, capital expenditure on scientific research, etc.; (2) Current year business loss; (3) Brought forward business loss under section 72; (4) Unabsorbed depreciation under section 32(2).

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.explanation: As per section 71(3A), where the net result of computation under the head 'Income from house property' is a loss, the assessee can set off such loss against income under any other head to the extent of Rs. 2,00,000 in any assessment year.

options: No, loss under the head 'Salaries' cannot be set off against income under any other head
Yes, only against income from house property
plain.explanation: Under the Income-tax Act, 1961, there cannot be a negative income from salary under normal circumstances, but even if a computational loss arises under the head 'Salaries' (e.g., allowances exceeding income), it cannot be set off against income under any other head under section 71.

plain.explanation: Under section 73(4), speculation loss can be carried forward for a maximum of 4 assessment years immediately succeeding the assessment year for which the loss was first computed.

options: Profits and gains of business or profession
plain.explanation: Brought forward business loss under section 72 can be set off only against profits and gains of business or profession.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a registered firm (partnership firm) carry forward and set off its business losses?
options: No, partnership firms cannot carry forward losses
Yes, the firm itself carries forward and sets off the loss against its own future business income
No, the loss must be allocated to partners for carry forward
Yes, but only unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward by the firm
plain.explanation: A partnership firm (whether registered or not) is a separate assessable entity. Business losses are carried forward by the firm itself to be set off against its future business profits, and not by the partners (except in case of dissolution/discontinuation where specific rules apply).

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What happens to the unabsorbed depreciation when there is no business income in the current year, but the assessee has income from capital gains and other sources?
options: It can be set off against capital gains and other sources
It can be set off against salary income only
It can be carried forward indefinitely, but first must be set off against any other head of income in the current year
plain.explanation: Under section 32(2), if unabsorbed depreciation cannot be fully set off against business income in the current year, it is added to the depreciation of the next year. However, in the current year, it can be set off against any other head of income (except salary) after inter-head adjustments are exhausted.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a loss from an exempt source of income be set off against taxable income?
options: No, since the income itself is exempt, any related loss cannot be set off against taxable income
Yes, provided books of accounts are audited
plain.explanation: Since the income from an exempt source does not form part of total income, any loss incurred from such exempt source cannot be set off against taxable income.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In the event of the death of an assessee, can the legal representative carry forward and set off the business losses of the deceased assessee?
options: Yes, the legal representative can carry forward and set off the deceased's business losses
No, business losses lapse upon the death of the assessee
Yes, but only for a maximum of 1 year
No, only unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward by the legal representative
plain.explanation: Under the Income-tax Act, business losses of the deceased assessee cannot be carried forward and set off by the legal representative, because the legal representative is not the same assessee who incurred the loss. (Note: This is an exception compared to inheritance of businesses where succession rules apply differently, but personal business loss under Sec 72 lapses upon death).

They can be set off against any other income under the same head or any other head under inter-source and inter-head rules
They can only be carried forward for 8 years
They lapse immediately and cannot be set off even within the same head
plain.explanation: Losses under the head 'Income from Other Sources' (general sources, e.g., loss on maintenance of machinery let out) can be set off against any other income under the same head (inter-source) and against any other head of income (inter-head) under sections 70 and 71, and cannot be carried forward.

Only unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward, not business loss

Yes, provided the loss was computed and returned when the business was active, and the 8-year time limit has not expired
No, unless the business is restarted in the current year

options: Yes, business loss can be set off against capital gains
No, business loss cannot be set off against capital gains under section 71
Yes, if capital gains are short-term only

Option 1 says 'No, business loss cannot be set off against capital gains'. That is incorrect because business loss CAN be set off against capital gains. scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage:
Mr. Raghav, an individual resident in India, furnishes the following details of his income and losses for the Financial Year 2025-26 (A.Y. 2026-27): 
1. Loss from speculative business A: Rs. 60,000
2. Profit from speculative business B: Rs. 90,000
3. Loss from non-speculative textile business: Rs. 1,50,000
4. Profit from non-speculative readymade garments business: Rs. 80,000
5. Loss from self-occupied house property: Rs. 2,50,000
6. Income from other sources (interest on fixed deposits): Rs. 3,00,000
He files his return of income on 28th July 2026.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the net taxable income or loss from speculative businesses after inter-source adjustment for Mr. Raghav for A.Y. 2026-27?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 70(1), loss from speculative business A (Rs. 60,000) can be set off against profit from speculative business B (Rs. 90,000). The net result is a profit of Rs. 30,000 from speculative businesses.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the treatment of the loss from the non-speculative textile business (Rs. 1,50,000) after inter-source adjustment with readymade garments business?
options: Entire loss of Rs. 1,50,000 is set off against garments profit, leaving a net business loss of Rs. 70,000
Textile business loss of Rs. 1,50,000 is set off against garments business profit of Rs. 80,000, leaving a business loss of Rs. 70,000 to be carried forward or set off against other heads
Textile business loss cannot be set off against garments business profit
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 70, loss from non-speculative textile business (Rs. 1,50,000) can be set off against profit from readymade garments business (Rs. 80,000), leaving a net business loss of Rs. 70,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the maximum amount of loss from house property that Mr. Raghav can set off against his interest income under other heads in A.Y. 2026-27?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 71(3A), the loss from house property that can be set off against income under any other head in any assessment year is restricted to a maximum of Rs. 2,00,000. The remaining Rs. 50,000 must be carried forward under section 71B.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Considering that Mr. Raghav filed his return on 28th July 2026, can he carry forward the unabsorbed house property loss of Rs. 50,000?
options: No, because the return was filed after 31st July
Yes, because filing return within due date is not mandatory for carrying forward house property loss
No, house property loss cannot be carried forward under any circumstance
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 80 mandates timely filing under section 139(1) for carrying forward business losses, capital losses, etc., but house property loss under section 71B and unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward even if the return of income is filed belatedly.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage:
M/s. Apex Enterprises (a partnership firm) has two manufacturing units (Unit 1 and Unit 2) and a speculative trading division. For the P.Y. 2025-26, the financial results are as under:
- Profit from Unit 1 (manufacturing): Rs. 4,00,000
- Loss from Unit 2 (manufacturing): Rs. 6,50,000
- Loss from speculative trading division: Rs. 1,20,000
- Brought forward business loss of Unit 1 from P.Y. 2022-23: Rs. 1,00,000
- Unabsorbed depreciation pertaining to Unit 2 from P.Y. 2024-25: Rs. 80,000.
The firm filed its return of income on time.

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the business income of M/s. Apex Enterprises after inter-source set-off of current year manufacturing losses and profits?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 70, current year loss from Unit 2 (Rs. 6,50,000) is set off against current year profit of Unit 1 (Rs. 4,00,000), resulting in a net current business loss of Rs. 2,50,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: How should the brought forward business loss of Rs. 1,00,000 from P.Y. 2022-23 be treated in P.Y. 2025-26?
options: It can be set off against current year business profits, but since there is a net current business loss, it is carried forward further
It lapses because current year has a loss
It can be set off against speculative trading profit
It can be set off against partner's salary
linkedMcqs.explanation: Brought forward business loss under section 72 can only be set off against business profits. Since the current year results in a net business loss, brought forward business loss cannot be set off and must be carried forward for the remaining years.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the treatment of the speculative trading loss of Rs. 1,20,000 incurred by the firm?
options: It can be set off against Unit 1's manufacturing profit
It can be set off against the net business loss
It cannot be set off against manufacturing profits and must be carried forward for up to 4 assessment years
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 73, speculation loss cannot be set off against non-speculation business income (manufacturing profit). It must be carried forward to be set off against speculation profits in subsequent years for a maximum of 4 assessment years.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: How is the unabsorbed depreciation of Rs. 80,000 treated?
options: It lapses due to lack of business profit
It can be added to current year unabsorbed depreciation and carried forward indefinitely, or set off against any other head of income (except salary) if available
It can only be carried forward for 8 years
It must be allocated to partners
linkedMcqs.explanation: Unabsorbed depreciation under section 32(2) can be carried forward indefinitely. In the current year, after inter-source and inter-head adjustments, it can be absorbed against other heads of income (except salary) or carried forward.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage:
Mr. Karan furnishes the following particulars of capital gains and losses for the Assessment Year 2026-27:
- Short-term capital gain (STCG) on sale of shares: Rs. 1,50,000
- Short-term capital loss (STCL) on sale of land: Rs. 2,40,000
- Long-term capital gain (LTCG) on sale of building: Rs. 90,000
- Long-term capital loss (LTCL) on sale of gold: Rs. 60,000
- Brought forward short-term capital loss from A.Y. 2023-24: Rs. 50,000.
He has no income under any other head and filed his return within the due date under section 139(1).

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the net short-term capital loss/gain after inter-source set-off for A.Y. 2026-27 (excluding brought forward losses)?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 70(2), short-term capital loss on sale of land (Rs. 2,40,000) can be set off against short-term capital gain on sale of shares (Rs. 1,50,000), resulting in a net short-term capital loss of Rs. 90,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the net long-term capital gain/loss after inter-source set-off for A.Y. 2026-27?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 70(3), long-term capital loss on sale of gold (Rs. 60,000) can be set off against long-term capital gain on sale of building (Rs. 90,000), resulting in a net long-term capital gain of Rs. 30,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can the net short-term capital loss of Rs. 90,000 be set off against the net long-term capital gain of Rs. 30,000 in the same assessment year?
options: No, short-term capital loss cannot be set off against long-term capital gain
Yes, short-term capital loss can be set off against both short-term and long-term capital gains
Yes, but only up to Rs. 10,000
No, capital losses cannot be set off against capital gains at all
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 70, a short-term capital loss can be set off against any capital gain, whether short-term or long-term. Thus, STCL of Rs. 90,000 can be set off against LTCG of Rs. 30,000, leaving a net short-term capital loss of Rs. 60,000 for the year.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the total capital loss to be carried forward by Mr. Karan to A.Y. 2027-28 (including brought forward STCL)?
options: Rs. 1,10,000 (Current net STCL of Rs. 60,000 + Brought forward STCL of Rs. 50,000)
Nil, as capital losses cannot be carried forward
linkedMcqs.explanation: Current year net STCL is Rs. 60,000. Brought forward STCL from A.Y. 2023-24 is Rs. 50,000 (which can be carried forward for 8 years under section 74). Both are carried forward under section 74, totaling Rs. 1,10,000.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage:
XYZ Ltd., a closely held domestic company, has the following income/loss details for A.Y. 2026-27:
- Business loss (computed) for P.Y. 2025-26: Rs. 8,00,000
- Brought forward business loss from P.Y. 2021-22: Rs. 3,00,000
- Brought forward unabsorbed depreciation from P.Y. 2023-24: Rs. 2,50,000
- Income from house property: Rs. 5,00,000
- Dividend income: Rs. 1,00,000
During P.Y. 2025-26, there was a change in shareholding, and shareholders holding 60% of voting power on 31-3-2021 were not the same persons holding 60% of voting power on 31-3-2026 (none of the statutory exemptions apply).

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is the brought forward business loss of Rs. 3,00,000 from P.Y. 2021-22 allowed to be carried forward and set off in view of the change in shareholding?
options: Yes, because business losses are never restricted by shareholding changes
No, because more than 51% of voting power has changed hands, violating section 79
Yes, because unabsorbed depreciation and business losses follow identical rules
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 79 provides that loss incurred in any year prior to the previous year cannot be carried forward and set off if there is a change in shareholding exceeding 49% (i.e., less than 51% voting power held by same persons). Hence, the brought forward business loss of Rs. 3,00,000 lapses.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the status of the brought forward unabsorbed depreciation of Rs. 2,50,000 in light of the change in shareholding under section 79?
options: It lapses entirely along with the business loss
It is not affected by section 79 and can be carried forward / set off
It can only be set off against house property income
It can be carried forward for only 8 years
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 79 restricts the carry forward and set off of business losses due to changes in shareholding, but it does NOT apply to unabsorbed depreciation under section 32(2). Unabsorbed depreciation remains fully eligible.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can XYZ Ltd. set off its current year business loss of Rs. 8,00,000 against its house property income of Rs. 5,00,000 under inter-head adjustment?
options: Yes, business loss can be set off against house property income
No, business loss cannot be set off against house property income under section 71
No, because business losses cannot be set off against any other head
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 71(2), business loss can be set off against income under any other head except 'Salaries'. Therefore, current year business loss of Rs. 8,00,000 can be set off against house property income of Rs. 5,00,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the remaining business loss of XYZ Ltd. to be carried forward to A.Y. 2027-28 after setting off against house property income?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Current year business loss is Rs. 8,00,000. It is set off against house property income of Rs. 5,00,000. The remaining unabsorbed current year business loss is Rs. 3,00,000, which can be carried forward under section 72 (since section 79 applies only to losses of *prior* previous years, not current year business loss).

sourceRef.chapterTitle: Aggregation of Income, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the aggregate loss from house property for Mr. Subhash for P.Y. 2025-26?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Loss from House Property A (Rs. 1,50,000) and Loss from House Property B (Rs. 1,80,000) are first aggregated under inter-source adjustment (section 70), resulting in a total house property loss of Rs. 3,30,000.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the maximum amount of house property loss that can be set off against salary and other sources in A.Y. 2026-27?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under section 71(3A), house property loss can be set off against other heads of income up to a maximum limit of Rs. 2,00,000 in any assessment year. The remaining Rs. 1,30,000 must be carried forward under section 71B.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can Mr. Subhash set off his business loss of Rs. 3,00,000 against his salary income of Rs. 7,00,000?
options: Yes, business loss can be set off against salary income without limit
No, business loss cannot be set off against salary income under section 71(2)
Yes, if the business was closed down
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 71(2) explicitly prohibits setting off business loss against income under the head 'Salaries'. Therefore, business loss cannot be set off against salary and must be carried forward under section 72.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: How should the loss from card games of Rs. 40,000 be treated?
options: It can be set off against interest on bank deposits
It can be set off against salary income up to Rs. 2,00,000
It cannot be set off against any income nor can it be carried forward
It can be carried forward for 4 years
linkedMcqs.explanation: Losses from card games, lotteries, races, or any other form of gambling cannot be set off against any income (not even against lottery winnings), nor can they be carried forward.
